title: Granite from six miles down
text: Most of the southern half of the Sierra Nevada is made of granite and other plutonic rocks of Mesozoic age. That granite was emplaced about 6 miles below the surface. The Sierra Nevada batholith pushed into strongly deformed but weakly metamorphosed sedimentary and volcanic rocks of Paleozoic and early Mesozoic age, known as the framework rocks.
